clue.text: Rank ivy choking short bough's vitality

indicators.note: the scrambled ivy grips the shortened bough, wrapping round it as a container
rank as an adjective means overgrown and wild, so the letters of ivy run riot into a new order
short means the word for a bough loses its final letter

parts.note: a bough is a branch of a tree

explanation.surface: Overgrown ivy strangling a stunted tree branch saps its life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' reads as a noun but is the adjective for overgrown; 'short' shortens the bough's word and 'choking' wraps the jumbled ivy round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrancy is liveliness and energy, the same quality as vitality.

clue.text: Stalwart and strict, against usurping king

indicators.note: a usurper takes another's throne, so the letter for against seizes the place of the letter for king

parts.note: strict means rigorous
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)
V is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: A tough character described as strict, opposing a king who seizes power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'usurping' swaps the first R of RIGOROUS for V.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone robust, strong and energetic.

clue.text: Ring — a way to identify a bird

parts.note: to give someone a ring is to give them a buzz on the phone
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A ringed band on the leg is how birdwatchers tell one bird from another.
explanation.definitionFit: The buzzard is a large bird of prey, a kind of hawk.

clue.text: A cry's raised in the passage

indicators.note: in a down entry raising a word means writing it from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a yell is a cry

explanation.surface: A shout goes up in the corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley is a narrow lane or passageway between buildings.

clue.text: He might well fall to pieces!

definitions.text: He might well fall to pieces!

parts.words: He might well fall to pieces!
parts.note: the surface suggests a man about to break down; the pieces are the kings, queens and pawns on a board, to which a losing competitor falls

explanation.surface: A man on the verge of a nervous collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: In a game of chess a competitor may be defeated by his opponent's men, the pieces.

clue.text: Inferior meat Cliff's put in steamer?

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside another, here the cliff inside the steamer

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a crag is a cliff; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A man called Cliff has been packed aboard a steamboat with some poor cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrag is the bony neck of mutton, a cheap cut; 'Cliff's' reads as a man's name but is a rock face.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag ends are the cheap scrawny neck cuts of mutton or veal.

clue.text: Analysing lines in painting

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for lines inside the word for painting

parts.note: coating is applying paint over a surface
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An art critic examining the brushstrokes in a canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Collating means gathering and comparing data in detail, a kind of analysis.

clue.text: This could yield one good fish

definitions.text: This could yield one good fish

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Some activity that might land a decent catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces AN, G and LING say 'one good fish', and the whole clue describes the sport that catches one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with rod and line is the pastime that brings in a catch.

clue.text: Fallen star's over the horizon

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed over another sits above it, coming first

parts.note: the sun is a star
ken is the range of one's knowledge, one's mental horizon

explanation.surface: A celebrity's career has dipped out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts SUN above KEN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sunken has sunk or dropped down to a lower level.

clue.text: Creatures keep an eye on wheeling hawk

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily

indicators.note: wheeling means turning round, so the word for hawk is read backwards

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: Animals watching a bird of prey circling overhead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeling' turns SELL into LLES. Hawk is the verb, peddle, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles are graceful antelopes, examples of animals.

clue.text: Its contents will get Jack quite drunk?

definitions.text: Its contents will get Jack quite drunk?

parts.words: Its contents will get Jack quite drunk?
parts.note: Jack seems a man who is to get tipsy; a jack is also a leather drinking vessel, and a large container of wine can be drained by drinking

explanation.surface: Some vessel of booze that will leave a man named Jack the worse for wear.
explanation.walkthrough: A jack was an old leather jug for ale, so the vessel and the drinker share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large bottle or jug for wine or cider.

clue.text: Understand yen for game

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Grasping that Japanese money is needed to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' is the adjective, as in 'game for anything', not a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Being game means being willing, prepared for action.

clue.text: All marks come up for review

parts.note: the sum is the total, all of something
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
to arise is to come up

explanation.surface: Every grade a student earns is up for reassessment.
explanation.definitionFit: To review a matter can mean to go over its main points briefly.

clue.text: Part of course presenting a hairy aspect

explanation.surface: A dish on the menu that gives one a whiskery look.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamb chops served as part of a main course of a meal; also the name for long side-whiskers widening on the cheeks.

clue.text: Unmentionable habits, generally speaking

parts.note: the surface suggests vices never spoken of; habits are garments, and unmentionables is a coy word for what is worn beneath

explanation.surface: Shameful personal vices, described in vague terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear, worn beneath outer garments, is coyly called one's unmentionables.

clue.text: A shining example?

parts.note: the phrase usually means a model to copy; here it is something that shines, giving off energy

explanation.surface: A model of good conduct held up for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy given off as light or heat, as a glowing body does when it shines.

clue.text: A body-builder's heavenly body

parts.note: anabolic steroids are drugs some bodybuilders take to build muscle

explanation.surface: A muscle-man's physique is so impressive it seems divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroids are small rocky bodies orbiting the sun, in space.

clue.text: Dodgy Liberal dangles precariously and becomes a pest

indicators.note: precariously suggests something unstable and tumbling, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A shady Liberal politician hangs on insecurely and turns into a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'precariously' rearranges DODGY, L and DANGLES.
explanation.definitionFit: The crane fly, known by this nickname, has larvae that damage lawns and crops.

clue.text: Rambling sort, the German, full of crack

indicators.note: full of means the German article holds the crack inside it

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a rift is a crack or split

explanation.surface: A wandering vagrant from Germany who is high on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is a person who roams from place to place without settling.

clue.text: Situation's primitive, overlooking a lake

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letters for a lake are ignored

parts.note: elemental means basic, primitive
A plus L, the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A primeval scene with a view across some water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' drops AL from the end of ELEMENTAL. It looks like a view, not an omission.
explanation.definitionFit: One's element is the natural environment or setting one thrives in.

clue.text: Composes masses

explanation.surface: Someone writing for large numbers of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music in full form for instruments; and a great many of something, lots.

clue.text: Gallant or snappy about uncouth rival?

indicators.note: about means the word for snappy goes round the rest

parts.note: chic means stylish, snappy as in a snappy dresser

indicators.note: uncouth means rough and unpolished, so the word rival is knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A well-dressed suitor contrasted with his boorish rival in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snappy' means smartly dressed here, not bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalric conduct is courteous and gallant like a knight's.

clue.text: Thread, note, securing border

indicators.note: securing means holding something firm within, so the note encloses the border

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A sewing note on fastening a fabric edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Thread here is a line of argument, not cotton.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the main subject running through a work, like a thread.

clue.text: Reserve, endless reserve, is socially not on

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's reserve force of volunteer soldiers

indicators.note: endless means the second word for reserve loses its final letter

parts.note: to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Coolness and reticence are frowned upon in polite company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims BOOK to BOO. The TA, the Territorial Army, is the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom is unacceptable in society.

clue.text: Line confined to shipman in the main?

definitions.text: Line confined to shipman in the main?

indicators.note: confined to means the line is shut up inside the sailor
in the main means mostly, so most of the word for shipman is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rating is a sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: A rope used only by sailors out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' trims RATING to RATIN, and 'confined to' puts L inside; the main is also the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are the small ropes forming steps on a ship's shrouds, used by sailors at sea.

clue.text: Top cover accordingly takes King at end of card game

indicators.note: takes means the word for accordingly holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: so means accordingly, therefore

indicators.note: at end of places the king after the card game

parts.note: ombre is an old card game for three
R is short for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A hat is therefore claimed as a prize by the winning king in a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Ombre is a seventeenth-century card game; 'Top cover' means something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat is something worn on the head.

clue.text: Confess about price leap

indicators.note: about means the word for confess goes round the price

parts.note: to sing is slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: Owning up to a sudden hike in prices.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is underworld slang for informing or confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump or bound.

clue.text: Divers in seas trod about

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters of seas and trod are mixed up

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers walking around in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' looks like swimmers but is the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old word for several different kinds, varied.
